finding: No source gives the number generating on 31 Dec 2022. Ørsted: first power April 2022; 48 turbines installed (H1 2022 report, Aug 2022); 71 installed (Q3 2022 report, 1 Nov 2022); annual report 2022 (1 Feb 2023) gives no count, only 'generated first power in April' and 'delays ... with the commissioning of turbines'. Energy Bureau count via CNA 29 Jan 2023: about 31 turbines not completed from 2022 (i.e. ~80 of 111 completed at year-end). Ørsted Q1 2023 report (3 May 2023): 97 installed, of which only 25 fully commissioned. So at end-2022 roughly 71-80 turbines stood, but fewer than 25 were fully commissioned (Ørsted definition: producing under the subsidy); the number merely energised/first-powered is not published. Year-end 2022 grid-connected capacity cannot be sourced; closest: <25 commissioned (<200 MW) by early May 2023.
confidence: low for a year-end figure; the bracketing sources themselves are reliable

finding: No exact 31 Dec 2023 figure. Ørsted H1 2023 report (Aug 2023): 97 installed, 69 fully commissioned. Ørsted 9M 2023 report (1 Nov 2023): 100 installed, 89 commissioned 'and thus fully producing power under the subsidy' (89 × 8 = 712 MW). Ørsted 30/31 Jan 2024: 107 installed, 'nearly 85 per cent' connected to the grid, 'approximately 700 MW' (~94 turbines). Last four turbines installed Feb 2024; all 111 connected by 3 Apr 2024; inaugurated 25 Apr 2024. Best estimate for end-2023: about 89-94 turbines, ~700-750 MW grid-connected; Ørsted's own rounded figure of 'approximately 700 MW' (nearly 85 %) dated 30 Jan 2024 is the closest published number.
confidence: medium-high (bracketed within ~5 turbines by Ørsted's own reports)
